title: Our Lord, Who Knows Full Well
description: Our Lord, Who Knows Full Well in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 9 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 106, “The importunate widow Lk 18:1-7”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our Lord, who knows full well The heart of ev-ery saint; In-vites us, by a pa-ra-ble, To pray and nev-er faint.

lines: Our Lord, who knows full well
Yet we must wait, till he appear,
He bids us never give him rest,
And gained, at last, her end.
Nor God, nor man, did he regard,
She urged him day and night,
At length he said, "I'll do her right,
Yes, though he may awhile forbear,
He'll help them from on high.
When they are grieved, his bowels move,
And makes our cause his care.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
